Edem subkutanog masnog tkiva anteromedijalne strane koljena dok je intenzitet signala
muskulature u regiji skeniranja uredan.
Zglobna tijela femorotibijalnog zgloba su primjereno oblikovana i kongurentna, zglobne hrskavice
se doimaju intaktne.
Mrljaste zone edema kosti, predomintano u području lateralnog femoralnog kondila i distalne
metafizedijafize femura, odgovarajući stanju po kontuziji, bez znakova frakture.
Prisutna je lateralna patelarna dislokacija uz prekinut tijek medijalnog patelarnog retinakula u
smislu kompletne rupture dok je tijek lateralnog patelarnog retinakula serpginozan, bez
evidnetnih znakova za rupturu navedenog.
Intenzitet signala koštane strukture patele je uredan.
Prednja i stražnja ukrižena sveza su primjerenog intenziteta signala, održanog tijeka, bez
znakova rupture.
Umjerena količina izljeva uz medijalnu kolateralnu svezu koja je u svom početnom tijeku i
izmjenjenog intenziteta signala, odgovarajući većoj parcijalnoj rupturi.
Lateralna kolateralna sveza se doima održanog tijeka.
Izmjenjen je intenzitet signala tetive popliteusa u završnom tijeku odgovarajući parcijalnoj
rupturi.
Izmjenjen je i intenzitet signala tetive m. semimembranozusa u završnom tijeku, neposredno
pred inserciju, moguće odgovarajući parcijalnoj leziji.
Izmjenjen je intenzitet signala trupa i stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska, odgovarajući
horizontalnoj rupturi.
Lateralni menisk se je primjerenog morfološkog izgleda.
Uredan je intenzitet signala završnog dijela tetive m. kvadricepsa femoria i ligamenta patele.
Umjerena količina slobodne tekućine supra i retropatelarno kao i u lateralnom recesusu.
Primjeren izgled Hoffine masti.
Nema znakova disrupcije vaskularnih struktura u zakoljenskoj jami.

The study reveals normal knee joint alignment.   No fracture is seen.  
  Minimal amount of joint effusion is seen.  
  MCL is intact.  Medial meniscus is not torn.  
  FCL, popliteus and biceps femoris tendons are preserved.       
  There is small size posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with suspected anteriorly flipped displaced meniscal fragment closed to the anterior horn. 
  Focal high grade partial thickness cartilage defect, about 6.5x17mm. at posterior part of the lateral meniscus, without subchondral bone lesion, is detected. 
 Normal course with preserved signal of the ACL is noted.  The PCL is intact.  
 The PF joint surface is preserved.   No subchondral bone lesion is noted.  
 The quadriceps and patellar tendons are preserved.     Evidence tear at posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with anteriorly flipped meniscal fragment closed to the anterior horn. 
  High grade, partial thickness cartilage defect, about 6.5x17mm. at posterior part of the lateral meniscus, without subchondral bone lesion.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female with trauma during ski accident 1.5 weeks ago with persistent pain, swelling and limited range of motion of left knee.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is a complete tear of the midportion of the anterior cruciate ligament. No normal intact fibers are identified. There is a borderline anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment at about 5 mm. There are bone contusions seen at the lateral femoral sulcus in the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau consistent with kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is a discrete region of linear low T1 signal along the posterior rim of the lateral tibial plateau which may indicate presence of an undisplaced lateral tibial plateau rim fracture.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

There is abnormal signal surrounding the medial collateral ligament at its origin along its course proximal to the medial joint line consistent with grade 2 sprain. There is significant disruption of the deep fibers with intact superficial fibers extending distally. The posterior oblique ligament appears intact. There is an associated partial thickness sprain of the femoral insertion of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact. There is some subtle increased signal seen in the proximal fibers of the fibular collateral ligament which could indicate presence of a low-grade sprain. The fibular collateral ligament, IT band, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is abnormal increased T2 signal seen in the periphery of the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body consistent with a meniscocapsular avulsion injury. No discrete surfacing meniscal tear is identified to the medial meniscus. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is unremarkable. As noted the medial patellofemoral ligament at its femoral insertion demonstrates a partial thickness sprain. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is reasonably well-maintained apart from some mild fissuring seen to the trochlear articular cartilage at the apex and involving the medial facet. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a moderate to large knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION:
 
Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with bone contusions corresponding to a pivot shift mechanism of injury and with possible undisplaced posterior tibial plateau fracturing. Plain film correlation is recommended.

Grade 2 medial collateral ligament sprain associated with partial-thickness sprain of the insertional fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

Evidence of meniscocapsular injury to the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body with no discrete surfacing tear identified.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Moderate knee effusion.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Mild interval reduction in moderate joint effusion. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Unchanged multidirectional tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with longitudinal horizontal and complete radial components. Unchanged mild meniscal extrusion. Unchanged displacement of the posterior medial meniscal root into the medial aspect of the intercondylar notch. This represents an unstable meniscal tear.
Normal medial collateral ligament. Partial-thickness fissuring of medial compartment articular cartilage.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Normal meniscus. Normal lateral collateral ligament complex. Unchanged partial-thickness chondral fissuring within the lateral compartment.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Unchanged complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is approximately 9 mm of anterior tibial translation. Normal posterior cruciate ligament.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Partial-thickness chondral fissuring within the medial and lateral patellar facet articular cartilage.
Normal extensor mechanism. Normal fat pads.

Bones:
Interval resolution of bone marrow edema previously seen within the posterolateral tibial plateau

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Small T1 hyperintense fluid collection within the muscle belly of the medial head of gastrocnemius measuring maximally up to 1 cm in craniocaudal dimension, is likely a small intramuscular hematoma.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.No significant interval change other than for resolution of posterolateral tibial plateau bone marrow edema compared to the previous MRI.
2.Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
3.Unchanged unstable tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with displacement of the posterior medial meniscal root into the medial intercondylar notch.

Γραµµοειδές παθολογικό σήµα στο οπίσθιο κέρας του έσω µηνίσκου. Συνυπάρχει διάχυτο παθολογικό σήµα καθόλη την έκταση του έσξ µηνίσκου στο πλαίσιο εκτεταµένης εκφύλισης - εκφυλιστικής ρήξης. - Αναγνωρίζεται οίδηµα εκατέρωθεν του ακέραιου έσω πλαγίου συνδέσµου. Φυσιολογικά απεικονίζονται οι πλάγιοι και χιαστοί σύνδεσµοι. - Από τον έλεγχο του προσθίου διαµερίσµατος οι τένοντες επιγονατιδικός και τετρακέφαλος καθώς και η επιγονατίδα ελέγχονται εντός του φυσιολογικού. - Μικρή συλλογή υγρού παρατηρείται ενδοαρθρικά, ενώ από τον έλεγχο του εκτατικού µηχανισµού παρατηρείται µικρή συλλογή υγρού στον προεπιγονατιδικό θύλακα. - Εντός του φυσιολογικού ελέγχεται ο αρθρικός χόνδρος. - Με σήµα εντός του φυσιολογικού ελέγχεται ο οστικός µυελός.

FINDINGS:

Fractures:
None.

Joint alignment:
Normal.

Degenerative changes:
None.

Bone marrow signal:
Partially covered, well delineated lobulated lesion in the distal femoral diaphysis showing T2 hyperintense signal with internal areas of low signal likely corresponding to matrix calcification, in keeping with a benign enchondroma.

Anterior cruciate ligament: Normal.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Normal.
Medial collateral ligament: Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament complex: Normal.

Medial meniscus: Normal.
Lateral meniscus: Normal.

Extensor tendons: Normal.
Patellar retinacula: Mild retropatellar chondropathy at the lateral articulating surface. Focal area of T2 signal abnormality at the inferior lateral aspect of the patellofemoral joint, at the superior lateral portion of the infrapatellar fat pad. Overall findings in keeping with Hoffa's fat pad impingement syndrome.
Pes anserinus: Normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner: Normal.

Joint effusion: Small joint effusion.
Baker cyst: None.

Other significant findings:
None.

CONCLUSION:
*Findings of patellar tendon lateral femoral condyle friction syndrome (Hoffa's fat pad impingement syndrome) as described above.
*Partially visualized distal femoral diaphysis enchondroma.

Tricompartmental articular cartilage surfaces are otherwise well preserved.

MRI  KNEE  -  RIGHT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Right knee pain, instability, ?meniscal injury vs ACL pathology as per <[Title]> <[Name]>.

COMPARISON:  [Date].

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

Tiny hairline undersurface tear involving posterior horn lateral meniscus. Medial meniscus is intact. 

ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL are intact.

Trace volume joint effusion.

Scattered areas of high-grade chondrosis with underlying bone edema at the patellofemoral compartment. Full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibiofemoral compartment.

No fracture or dislocation.

Extensor mechanism is intact. Quadriceps and patellar tendon are intact.

Popliteal fossa cyst.

Soft tissue edema within the subcutaneous tissue anterior to the patella.

INTERPRETATION:
Tiny hairline undersurface tear of the posterior horn lateral meniscus.

Multiple foci of high-grade chondrosis with underlying bone marrow edema at the patellofemoral compartment as well as full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibiofemoral compartment. Findings are compatible with moderate OA.
